acceptance_criteria.criterion: GET /api/config/credentials returns an array of { id, label, host, token } objects with tokens masked via maskToken().
PUT /api/config/credentials with a new id (or no id) creates a new credential entry in the array.
PUT /api/config/credentials with an existing id updates (upserts) the existing entry.
PUT /api/config/credentials auto-generates the id from label in kebab-case when id is not provided in the body.
When the auto-generated ID already exists, a numeric suffix (-2, -3, ...) is appended until a free slot is found.
PUT /api/config/credentials rejects requests that would create duplicate IDs.
DELETE /api/config/credentials/:id removes the credential entry matching the given id.
All integration tests in src/server/__tests__/routes/config.test.ts for credential endpoints pass.

comments.note: The PUT route previously had a host validation guard (rejecting paths with slashes/whitespace and prototype-pollution keys). The new GitCredentialEntry model does not impose such restrictions on host — the host field is a plain string identifier and validation is left to the caller. If stricter host validation is desired in future (e.g. rejecting hosts with path separators), it can be added as a separate concern. Current behaviour is correct per spec.

buildMaskedCredentials() and generateUniqueId() are module-private helpers in config.ts. If more credential utility functions accumulate, consider extracting them to a dedicated src/server/routes/credential-utils.ts to keep config.ts focused on route registration.

The generateUniqueId() function falls back to 'credential' when toKebabCase(label) returns an empty string (all-special characters). A more descriptive fallback (e.g. 'unnamed-credential') could improve usability in edge cases.

summary: Reviewed 2 files (src/server/routes/config.ts, src/server/__tests__/routes/config.test.ts) plus supporting utilities (requestUtils.ts, config.ts, config.types.ts, slug.ts). 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 3 Medium and 2 Low observations recorded. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: MEDIUM — A02 (Cryptographic Failures) / A09 (Security Logging): Git tokens (Personal Access Tokens) are stored as plaintext in config.json on disk. This is an inherent design constraint (the tool must use the raw token to authenticate git operations), but it creates risk if the config file is world-readable or included in backups/version control. Recommendation: Ensure config.json is created with restrictive file permissions (0600) at install time, and add it to .gitignore. Consider adding a note in documentation. No code change required for WP-005.

MEDIUM — A09 (Security Logging & Monitoring Failures): PUT and DELETE /api/config/credentials endpoints mutate security-sensitive credentials (add, update, delete tokens) with no audit log. If unauthorized access to the config API occurs, there is no trail to detect it. Recommendation: Add structured log entries (e.g. 'Credential created: id=X', 'Credential deleted: id=X') on successful mutations, without logging token values. This is a systemic gap across the config routes, not specific to WP-005.

MEDIUM — A04 (Insecure Design): The host field in PUT /api/config/credentials accepts any non-empty string with no format or scheme validation. A previous guard (rejecting slashes, whitespace, prototype-pollution keys) was removed in WP-005 to accommodate the new GitCredentialEntry model. While the host field is not used in file-system operations or shell commands in this WP's scope, if downstream code uses host to construct git remote URLs or shell arguments without further sanitization, this could become a higher-severity injection vector. File: src/server/routes/config.ts, PUT /api/config/credentials handler (~line 200). Recommendation: Add lightweight host format validation (e.g. reject values containing path separators or URL scheme prefixes) as a defence-in-depth measure. Track for resolution before host values are used in any system calls.

LOW — A04 (Insecure Design): No maximum length constraint is applied to the label, host, token, or id string fields in PUT /api/config/credentials beyond the global 1 MB request body limit enforced by parseJsonBody(). An adversary with local access could store arbitrarily long strings that bloat config.json. Recommendation: Add per-field maximum length checks (e.g. label ≤ 200 chars, host ≤ 253 chars per DNS spec, token ≤ 1000 chars, id ≤ 100 chars). Low risk given local-only deployment context.

LOW — A03 (Injection / Information Exposure): The DELETE route echoes back the caller-supplied credId value in a 404 error message: 'No credential entry found with id "${credId}".'. This is not exploitable in a local-only deployment context, but reflects user-controlled input in error responses. Recommendation: Consider a generic message ('Credential not found.') or sanitize the echoed ID to a known-safe character set before inclusion in error text.

[documentation-forward] The registerConfigRoutes JSDoc endpoint table lists GET/PUT/DELETE /api/config/credentials but does not document the request body shape for PUT (specifically: `{ id?: string, label: string, host: string, token: string }`) or the response shape (masked GitCredentialEntry[]). Add a structured request/response schema to the JSDoc or a companion README section so future contributors can understand the API contract without reading the implementation.

[documentation-forward] The generateUniqueId() helper has a good one-line JSDoc but does not document the fallback behaviour when toKebabCase(label) returns an empty string (falls back to 'credential'). Add an @example or @remarks note to the function's JSDoc block covering this edge case, consistent with the level of detail in the toKebabCase docstring in slug.ts.

Maintainability: The PUT route has an excellent inline comment block (lines 157–168) that documents all three code paths. However, the upsert branch comment ('New entry with an explicit ID — no existing entry matches, so create.') doesn't clarify that this path also handles user-supplied IDs that were never auto-generated. This is a clarity gap, not a defect. Consider adding a parenthetical: '(treats the caller-supplied id as canonical — no uniqueness check needed since findIndex returned -1)' for future readers.

Architecture: buildMaskedCredentials() and generateUniqueId() are correctly scoped as module-private helpers. The current helper count (4 private helpers: maskToken, extractScheme, isValidFiniteInteger, buildMaskedCredentials, generateUniqueId) remains manageable within config.ts. If the credential surface grows (e.g., bulk import, ordering), the Developer's earlier suggestion to extract a credential-utils.ts module should be revisited. No action needed now.

Performance: generateUniqueId() constructs a new Set from existingCredentials.map() on every PUT call. This is O(n) and negligible given the expected cardinality of a credentials list (typically < 20 entries). No performance concern.
